steps.body: Seventeen, eighteen, nineteen fill the frame's neighbourhood almost to twenty. Nineteen is ten and nine — one dot shy of two full tens.
steps.narration: Seventeen, eighteen, nineteen fill the frame's neighbourhood almost to twenty. Nineteen is ten and nine — one dot shy of two full tens.

widget.prompt: A full group of 10 is already shown. Add the extra dots needed to make 18.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 8 dots still missing — the ten alone only makes 10, not 18.
7 leaves 1 dot still missing; ten and 7 is 17, one short of 18.
9 adds 1 too many; ten and 9 is 19, one past 18.

widget.missFeedback: The ten is done; count on from 10 while adding dots, and stop when you reach 18.
widget.successFeedback: 18 built — one complete ten and 8 more, exactly what the teen numeral says.

predict.prompt: Nineteen is one more dot away from…
predict.reveal: Nine ones is a nearly-finished second frame; one more dot completes it at twenty. The full first frame never goes away, so the count moves forward to twenty — not back to ten.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb 17 19.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb 17 19 rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: A group shows 19 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: Correct — a full ten and 9 more is what the numeral 19 says: 1 ten, 9 ones.
That numeral names one more dot than the group shows.
That numeral stops one dot short; the ten plus the extras reaches 19.
9 counts only the extras and forgets the whole completed ten underneath.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 15? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 15 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 16.
17 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 15 lands on 16.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 15: you land on 16.
widget.successFeedback: 16 — one hop forward; the teens follow the song exactly.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 16.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 15 means one hop, stopping on 16.

widget.prompt: Which pair is NOT a split of 18?

options.label: 10 and 9
options.feedback: Correct — 10 + 9 = 19, one too many, so this pair is not a split of 18.

options.label: 10 and 8
options.feedback: 10 + 8 = 18, so this pair is a valid split of 18 — the teen split itself.

options.label: 18 and 0
options.feedback: 18 + 0 = 18, so this pair is a valid split of 18, keeping everything in one part.

options.label: 17 and 1
options.feedback: 17 + 1 = 18, so this pair is a valid split of 18.
